canonical_question: How does the 5% re-melting strategy compare to other homogenization techniques like hot forging or annealing in terms of cost and grain size?

question_variants.question: How does the 5% re-melting strategy compare to other homogenization techniques like hot forging or annealing in terms of cost and grain size?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text mentions the 5% re-melting strategy (5 times) and its result, but provides no data on cost or grain size comparisons with hot forging or annealing.

answers.answer: The document notes each ingot was re-melted at least 5 times but does not provide comparative data on cost or grain size against hot forging or annealing.
answers.boundary_limitation: No comparative cost or grain size data.
evidence_spans: Fig. 1 shows the X-ray diffraction patterns of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr and HfMoTaTiZr 0.5 . HfMoTaTiZr is identified as a single-phase BCC crystal structure (cI2-W), which is identical to HfMoTaTiZr prepared by Juan et al. [20]
The shape of the (200), (211) and (220) peaks are asymmetric due to the compositional difference between dendrite and interdendrite regions.
The XRD-determined lattice parameters of HfMoTaTiZr and HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 are a HfMoTaTiZr = 3.392 Å and a HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 = 3.325 Å, respectively.
